body.html: The hardest question in coaching a full roster isn’t what to prescribe — it’s who to look at first. The daily priority list answers that one.

How it works

Overnight, augo reads the last seven days of data across every athlete you coach. By the morning a ranked list is waiting, showing something like “7 of 12” — the athletes who warrant a look today, not the whole roster.

Each entry carries a one-line reason, so you can tell at a glance why someone surfaced, and tap through to ask the assistant for more.

What it reads

  • Completed workouts and their metrics — pace, power, heart rate, duration, distance
  • Structured session feedback — feel, aches and pains, RPE, fuelling, written and voice notes
  • Coach–athlete chat messages
  • Your own private notes

Compared against themselves

Each athlete is measured against their own recent baseline rather than a population average. A 150bpm easy run means nothing in isolation; it means something if that athlete has run the same route at 138bpm for a month.

This is also why the list needs about a week of data before it is useful for a new athlete — there is no baseline to deviate from yet.

faqs.question: How often does the priority list update?
faqs.answer: It is rebuilt overnight, so a fresh ranked list is waiting each morning.

faqs.question: What data does it analyse?
faqs.answer: Completed workouts and their metrics, structured session feedback including voice notes, coach–athlete chat messages, and your own private coach notes.

faqs.question: Why is my priority list empty for a new athlete?
faqs.answer: augo compares each athlete against their own recent baseline, so it needs roughly a week of data before it can tell what is unusual for them.

faqs.question: Does it show my whole roster?
faqs.answer: No — only the athletes who warrant attention, shown as a count like "7 of 12".
